chunks: Sahl ibn Ziyād, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad ibn Abī Naṣr, from Dāwūd ibn al-Ḥuṣayn, from Abū al-ʿAbbās, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said:
I asked him about the mistake for which there are blood money and expiation: is it that a man intentionally strikes another man but does not intend to kill him? He said: “Yes.”
I said: If he shot at a sheep and struck a human being? He said: “That is the mistake about which there is no doubt; upon him are the blood money and the expiation.”

key_terms.الدِّيَةُ: financial compensation owed for causing death or injury
key_terms.الْخَطَإِ: accidental wrongdoing or unintentional harm in a legal context
key_terms.الْكَفَّارَةُ: prescribed expiation required for the offense
key_terms.رَمَى: he shot or threw at a target

ai.seo_question: When are blood money and expiation required in cases of accidental killing in Shia fiqh?
ai.summary: This hadith explains a legal ruling concerning accidental killing and the cases in which both blood money and expiation are due. It distinguishes between intending an act of striking without intending death, and a clearer accidental case such as aiming at an animal but striking a person, affirming liability in both cases.
